hypotheses.title: Along-front outlet-chi residual steps (a relational, not a scarp, signature)
layers: one elevation product (the 3DEP-10m-reduced pack or the official det_elev band)
the first-order basin graph already built by src/gems60/drains.py
hypotheses.signature: per first-order basin, the residual of outlet elevation against chi; order the residuals along the range-front strike and look for a step/offset - a fault crossing the front moves every outlet on one side out of the regional trend
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: it measures the discontinuity between adjacent drainage systems rather than the height of any scarp, so a fault whose scarp is buried or degraded still steps the along-front residual; the catalogue's faults are exactly those with mappable surface expression
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: H33-B uses valley-line collinearity, H33-A multi-physics orientation agreement and the H61 arm knickpoint density; nothing uses outlet-chi residuals ordered along a front, i.e. a statistic defined between basins rather than inside one

hypotheses.cost: low (~1 min CPU on the cached hydrology)
hypotheses.status: NOT RUN - queued behind the instrument repair (G61-5)

hypotheses.title: Thermal-anomaly-anchored conduit traces (INGENIOUS springs + travertine/sinter + 2 m probes)
layers: GDR 1391 spring & well chemistry (27,092 rows in the footprint; Na-K-Ca / silica geothermometers)
GDR 1391 paleo-geothermal travertine/sinter deposits (709 sites in the footprint)
GDR 1391 2 m temperature-probe anomalies (2,029 positive stations inside the footprint)
elevation-gradient lineament orientation (Horn slopes) as the shape prior
hypotheses.signature: lineaments that terminate at, or pass through, a thermal anomaly, weighted by the anomaly's distance from the mapped catalogue and by measured reservoir temperature
hypotheses.why_off_catalogue: fluid reaches the surface along a permeable fault; 15+ sites above 150 C lie >3 km from any mapped trace, so some unmapped structure must feed them, and a paleo-sinter or travertine body marks a conduit that need not be active today

The sibling repository's concealment prior used SGMC map-unit polygons, not the official cover-thickness raster.

hypotheses.mechanism: Recovers exact 10 m absolute steepness difference Δksn = ku - kd = (ksn_max + 0.5)*(1 - exp(-step_max)) across the 11-cell (110 m) moving-window reach, restricts candidate channels to bedrock-incising reaches (ksn_max >= 10 m^0.9, drainage_px_10m >= 200), couples with 10 m piedmont slope-break / incision contrast (0.25*pied_z), masks 4 named confounds (playa, deep basin fill, conductive clay, lithologic intrusive cores), and enforces >= 3 independent drainages (branch_sig_100m) along a common 22-azimuth strike corridor with 2.8 px (280 m) minimum-separation NMS.
hypotheses.why_missing_from_catalogue: USGS Qfaults and INGENIOUS regional compilations stop at range-front scarps where late-Holocene alluvial fans bury surface rupture or where distributed relay ramps split displacement across parallel piedmont strands; bedrock channels and incised fan heads preserve the base-level fall Δksn across multiple adjacent catchments along strike.
hypotheses.difference_from_existing: Fixes the fatal small-denominator log-ratio pathology in H65-1 (log((ku+0.5)/(kd+0.5)), where 39.6% of >2x steps occurred on flat washes with ksn < 10) and fixes the contiguous 13x5 corridor-brick quantization defect in src/gems60/lane.py via 280 m minimum-separation NMS.

hypotheses.status: PROPOSED — ranked #2 in Round H66/H67 tectonic-geomorphology slate
hypotheses.mechanism: Following Perron & Royden (2013), in steady-state uniform-rock uplift z(x) = z_b + (U/K)^n * χ(x); a dip-slip fault crossing multiple adjacent catchments introduces an iso-χ elevation offset Δz_χ between channels at matched χ above the shared piedmont base level z_b.
hypotheses.why_missing_from_catalogue: Catches eroded bedrock fault-line scarps and intrabasin horst-bounding faults that lack preserved Quaternary alluvial scarps in Qfaults.
hypotheses.difference_from_existing: Uses integral elevation difference at matched χ across neighboring basins rather than local derivative d(z)/d(χ) within a single reach.
hypotheses.cost: medium (requires common base-level re-anchoring across tile boundaries; see IR-65-TILE-01)

The rule was re-derived from the second instrument (cover the scatter-smoothed density) and now measures +0.0247 (12/12 draws) over the incumbent on the catalogue-aware variant. irregularities.statement: Two documents in this repository state DIFFERENT marginal bars for the same metric. src/gems32/metric.py and the passing test tests/test_metric.py::test_marginal_emission_rule_exact_single_truth_pixel say k > alpha*s = 0.0520 at s = 0.26. docs/research/score-ceiling-analysis.md section 1 states k > alpha*s/(1 - alpha*s) = 0.0549. The latter form does not follow from the metric: adding one unit of mass raises the denominator by EXACTLY alpha regardless of where it lands, giving k > alpha*s. A brute-force sweep over 300 random configurations agrees with the alpha*s form 300/300.
irregularities.mitigation: The exact theorem is stated, machine-verified in scripts/verify_theorems.py block (B), and used by src/gems32/emitter.py. NOTE the propagated consequence: the successor repository GEMSDOE28 uses tau_live = 0.05485 as its live break-even efficiency, which is 5.5% too high, biasing its pruning rule toward deleting dots that were still profitable.

irregularities.statement: The 'adaptive credit bar' that this project has repeatedly cited as its stopping rule CANNOT BIND on an emission confined to its own belief support. For a support pixel of a binary field, kbar(x) = sum_delta field(x+delta)k(delta) >= field(x)k(0) = 1, so the added false-positive mass 1 - kbar <= 0 and the acceptance inequality holds unconditionally for any s < 1/alpha = 5. Measured: emitter.emit(field, budget=None, prior_dti=0.26) consumes the ENTIRE 121,131-px H19-5 support and terminates with stopped_by='exhausted_support'.
irregularities.mitigation: Stated openly in knowledge/02 section 4b. The bar is still the correct rule for deciding whether a dot PAYS; it is simply not a constraint on an emission that never leaves its own support. Budget must therefore come from somewhere else -- which is exactly why the three-slot identification experiment that measures the hidden-set quantities is the next action rather than another budget sweep.

irregularities.title: 10 m log-ratio step_max = log((ku+0.5)/(kd+0.5)) is dominated by small-denominator ephemeral washes on basin floors, causing H65-1 E1 failure
irregularities.statement: In src/gems65/dem10.py, step_max was defined as log((ku+0.5)/(kd+0.5)) with a 0.5 m^0.9 additive floor and no minimum ksn requirement. Direct inspection of data/external/dem10_chi_100m_i16.tif shows that 39.6% of all pixels with step_max > ln(2) occur on flat basin floors where ksn_max < 10 m^0.9 (e.g. ku = 1.5, kd = 0.2 -> log-ratio = +1.05 despite Δksn = 1.3 m^0.9), whereas a genuine bedrock fault scarp with ku = 60, kd = 30 has a smaller log-ratio (+0.69) despite a 23x larger absolute steepness step (Δksn = 30 m^0.9).
irregularities.mitigation: scripts/build_dem10_cache.py (--mode h66) algebraically recovers the exact 10 m absolute steepness step Δksn = ku - kd = (ksn_max + 0.5)*(1 - exp(-step_max)) directly from bands 1 and 2 of dem10_chi_100m_i16.tif, enforces a bedrock-reach gate (ksn_max >= 10 m^0.9), and excludes ephemeral basin-floor washes (ksn_max < 10 & step_max > 0.5). E1 jumps from +0.0326 [-0.0144, +0.0790] (FAIL) to +0.4251 [+0.2253, +0.6273] (PASS, 158/262 positive) and HOLDOUT-DTI increases 5.68x (from 0.011576 to 0.065739).

irregularities.title: Un-thinned top_k_dots on 13x5 corridor paint emits contiguous rectangular bricks that waste 85% of the dot budget inside the 3-px DTI cover radius
irregularities.statement: src/gems60/lane.py paints each strike-aligned candidate with a 13x5 pixel corridor kernel and previously selected the top-k pixels directly via argpartition without spatial thinning. Because adjacent pixels inside a 13x5 corridor have nearly identical scores, top_k_dots emitted solid 5-pixel-wide bricks. Under the competition DTI metric (max_cover radius = 3 px = 300 m, alpha = 2.0), a single dot already covers a 7x7 neighborhood; packing 15-25 dots into the same 300 m radius adds zero TPw while multiplying FPw by 15-25x.
irregularities.mitigation: Added min_sep_px = 2.8 (280 m) greedy non-maximum suppression to top_k_dots in src/gems60/lane.py, distributing the 40,000-dot budget across ~3.5x more independent strike-aligned corridors and lifting HOLDOUT-DTI to 0.065739 [0.055715, 0.076201].
